data.reason:
The KPI's main goal is town-wide on_time_deliveries, with p95_wait_s, max_wait_s and unfinished as watched goals (K1). Option 1 does not improve the main goal: on-time goes from 81.0 to 80.8 (-0.2, 0/5 seeds improved). It also worsens the customer-facing metrics. Late rises from 1.6 to 1.8, p95_wait_s from 94.6 to 116, max_wait_s from 270 to 321, and blocked s from 888 to 1046. I follow the LLM's recommendation.

I am choosing against a unanimous yes vote. Customers do not vote. The KPI requires that changes worse for customers be justified, and a +1.3 utility gain for C (8.9 -> 10.2) does not justify consistently longer tail waits with no on-time gain. In D4 I committed to measuring a targeted mitigation for C 'instead of trading customer tail waits for it'. Option 1 is exactly that trade, so adopting it would break the stated form of the commitment rather than honour it.

I acknowledge that this is the fifth period without a real mitigation for C. C remains far behind A and B (8.9 vs about 25). That is a real cost to C's trust and to the operator's credibility, and I take responsibility for it on behalf of the operator.

The mitigation must still be delivered, through means that do not cost customers. Options are negotiated compensation, a rule aimed at C's specific bottleneck, or an intermediate hold_limit such as 55s measured per seed. Whether hold_limit should differ by season or demand level is left open until it has been measured in a busy period. The small drop in road violations (27.2 -> 26.0) does not outweigh the customer harm while its safety relevance is unexamined. No contract change is involved, so customers' promised times are unaffected.
assumptions: The quiet-period measurement on 5 seeds is representative of this period's demand.
The p95_wait_s and max_wait_s increases reflect a real effect rather than one or two outlier seeds.
C will continue participating cooperatively despite a further delay, if a concrete mitigation is measured soon.
The D4 commitment meant a mitigation that does not trade customer tail waits.
unknowns: Per-seed spread of p95_wait_s and max_wait_s under option 1.
Performance of an intermediate hold_limit (55s) for customers and for C.
The root cause of C's low utility (8.9) and whether a rule can target it.
How C will react to another delay of the promised mitigation.
Next period's demand level and whether a longer hold_limit behaves differently in busy periods.
Whether the road violation level is safety-relevant.
